_meta.project: instex Instrument Explorer -- TELESCOPES mode: Subaru Telescope 8.2 m (NAOJ), every focus and the entrance pupil
_meta.companion: data/telescopes/subaru.md (same content as Markdown). Structure: sources{key: cite, file, url}; subaru{title, telescope{primary, pupil_default, foci[] (each with its own pupil block)}, params, not_found, conflicts, notes}. Focus and pupil fields carry refs (subaru.<param>) into the sourced params.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/telescopes/subaru/, or an existing file already used by data/imaging/widefield.json (STP, A18, SSP, S15, SPFS, OBSS) or data/telescopes/magellan.json (HCI, HCIG) -- SAME FILE. derived = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). figure_readoff = a value read off a saved figure (not text-checkable; its caption/label quote is checked). INFERRED = reasoned, not stated by a source. NOT FOUND = gap. Nothing is filled from memory.
_meta.refs: Telescope-object refs name params as subaru.<id>.
_meta.check_result: 125 quotes machine-checked against the saved files' extracted text (pdftotext -layout, -raw and default for PDFs; tag-stripped text and raw source for HTML; .py as is): all pass (2026-10-19). 2 figure read-offs (FIGURE READ-OFF) are visual only; their label quotes are among the checked quotes.

telescope_design.value: alt-azimuth; modified Ritchey-Chretien with three interchangeable secondaries (Cassegrain f/12.2, Nasmyth f/12.6) plus a prime-focus unit; four foci
telescope_design.quote: The Subaru Telescope has an 8.2 m F/1.83 primary mirror with a focal length of 15 m. Three secondary mirrors are installed, each comprising a modified Ritchey–Cretien system at the F/12.2 Cassegrain or F/12.6 Nasmyth foci.

alternatives.quote: Basic Optics: Ritchey-Chretian System Foci: Four Primary focus: F2.0 (with corrector lens) Cassegrain focus: F12.2 Nasmyth focus (optical): F12.6 Nasmyth focus (infrared): F13.6
The Subaru Telescope has four focal points: the primary focus, the Cassegrain focus, and two Nasmyth foci.

telescope_design.note: Table 2 of I04 marks which configurations are Ritchey-Chretien (see rc_flags): the IR Nasmyth and the optical Nasmyth without image rotator are not.

primary_effective_diameter.quote: The finished mirror has a physical diameter of 8.3 m, a thickness of 20 cm and a weight of 22.8 tonnes. The diameter of the effective reflecting surface is 8.2 m, and the focal length is 15 m.

alternatives.quote: Effective diameter: 8.2 m
Effective diameter (diameter of light affecting area): 8.2 m (27 ft.)

primary_physical_diameter.quote: The finished mirror has a physical diameter of 8.3 m

alternatives.quote: The primary mirror blank, 8.3 m in diameter and 30 cm in thickness, was manufactured using Ultra Low Expansion (ULE) glass by Corning Incorporated
The latest realuminization of the 8.3 m primary mirror was conducted in 2003 August.

primary_physical_diameter.derived: DERIVED: (8.3 - 8.2)/2 = 0.05 m annulus outside the effective surface.

primary_meniscus.quote: monolithic, thin meniscus zero-expansion glass was adopted for the primary mirror. ... a support system consisting of 261 actuators distributed in 8 rings was adopted to support the mirror.

the actuators are inserted into “pockets” bored into the back of the blank at the 261 actuator locations

primary_radius_conic.note: 'Aspheric constant' = conic constant K (I04 Table 1); M02 lists the eccentricity squared e^2 = -K. Sign of R differs by convention.

design_history.value: primary enlarged from 7.5 m to 8.2 m late in the design with the radius of curvature kept, so the prime-focus ratio went from f/2.0 to f/1.83
design_history.quote: At the late stage of an engineering model study of the Subaru Telescope, it was decided to increase the size of the primary mirror from 7.5 m to 8.2 m. The radius of the curvature of the primary mirror was, however, kept unchanged so that the effects of this change on other design specifications became minimal. Accordingly, the F- ratio of the prime focus changed from 2.0 to 1.83

alternatives.quote: Conceptual planning for the 8.2 m (originally 7.5 m) Subaru Telescope began in the summer of 1984

design_history.note: Likely origin of the "F/2.0 (with corrector)" prime-focus value still on the observatory pages (see prime_focus_published_F).

first_light.value: engineering first light 1998 December 24; open use from 2000 December
first_light.quote: the engineering First Light of the Subaru Telescope was achieved on 1998 December 24.

secondary_mirrors.note: All three are convex hyperboloids (K < -1; the sign convention of I04 Table 1 gives both mirrors negative R). The IR M2 has the optical Cassegrain prescription but is smaller (1265 vs 1330 mm), and so becomes the aperture stop (see ir_secondary_stop).
secondary_mirrors.derived: DERIVED (paraxial, mirror equation, f2 = |R|/2): Opt/Cass s = 15000 - 12652.174 = 2347.826 mm, image 15652.17 mm from M2 -> 3000.0 mm behind the M1 vertex, m = 6.6667, f = 100000 mm (= Table 2). Opt/Nas at 12484.300 mm: image 4992.6 mm behind the vertex, f = 104207.1 mm (= Table 2 Nasmyth-optical with image rotator).

ir_secondary.value: IR M2: lightweight ULE, 185 kg, silver coated; tip-tilt and chopping (60" amplitude, up to 3 Hz, 80% duty cycle)
ir_secondary.quote: The tip-tilt and chopping infrared secondary mirror (Itoh et al. 1998) is made of light-weight ULE glass (185 kg) and has a silver coating. ... The maximum chopping frequency currently available is 3 Hz with a duty cycle of 80% and a position error of < 0. ′′ 1 rms.

alternatives.quote: The infrared secondary mirror has chopping and tip-tilt correction capabilities, which are useful for near-infrared observations and indispensable for mid-infrared observations.

ir_secondary_nasmyth_use.value: the IR M2 also serves the IR Nasmyth focus: it is moved along the optical axis and the primary figure is force-corrected; optical and IR M2s can be swapped between Nasmyth foci if needed
ir_secondary_nasmyth_use.quote: the infrared Cassegrain secondary can be used for observations at the infrared Nasmyth focus by moving the infrared secondary mirror along the optical axis and applying a force correction on the primary mirror shape. Although the coating and pupil size are different, the infrared secondary can be used for optical Nasmyth observations, and the optical secondary can be used for infrared Nasmyth observations, if necessary.
ir_secondary_nasmyth_use.derived: DERIVED (paraxial, IR M2 f2 = 2762.149 mm, solving for the Table 2 back focus): IR Nasmyth with image rotator (back focus 4600 mm) needs M1-M2 = 12619.7 mm -> f = 108512.4 mm; without rotator (4992.6 mm) 12612.4 mm -> f = 110605.2 mm; i.e. the IR M2 sits 33-40 mm closer to M1 than at the Cassegrain focus (12652.174 mm). Optical Nasmyth without rotator (4600 mm): Opt/Nas M2 at 12492.4 mm -> f = 102244.5 mm.

ir_secondary_stop.value: the IR M2 (1265 mm) is the aperture stop: pupil 8081.9 mm at the IR Cassegrain, 7971.6 / 7947.5 mm at the IR Nasmyth (with / without image rotator); 8200 mm at all optical foci
ir_secondary_stop.derived: DERIVED: an on-axis beam from the full 8.2 m primary has a footprint D (f1 - d)/f1 on the M2: 1283.5 mm at the Cassegrain spacing (fits the 1330 mm optical M2, overfills the 1265 mm IR M2) and 1375.2 mm on the 1400 mm Opt/Nas M2. Stop = 1265 x f1/(f1 - d): 8081.9 mm at 12652.174 mm (Table 2: 8081.9); 7971.6 mm at 12619.7 mm (7971.6); 7947.5 mm at 12612.4 mm (7947.5). The three published IR pupil diameters follow exactly from the 1265 mm IR M2.

prime_focus_corrector_2004.value: 30' field at F/2, images better than 0.23" to the edge, with a new ADC (Suprime-Cam era corrector)
prime_focus_corrector_2004.quote: An ambitious wide-field prime-focus corrector with a new type of atmospheric dispersion compensator (Nariai 1994) allows for a 30′ field of view at F/2 with an optical image quality of better than 0. ′′ 23, right up to the edge of the field.

prime_focus_location.value: prime focus 15 m above the primary mirror (at the top end, inside the prime focus unit)
prime_focus_location.quote: Subaru Telescope has the unique prime focus (主焦点) located 15 m above the primary mirror

alternatives.quote: The PFU is mounted and fixed on the top ring of the telescope. The interface between the telescope and the camera is a torus flange located behind the prime focus by 230 mm.

suprimecam_focus.value: Suprime-Cam: prime focus F/1.86 with a 3-lens Wynne-type corrector incl. ADC; 0.202"/15-um pixel; 34' x 27' mosaic, 30' unvignetted
suprimecam_focus.quote: Suprime-Cam covers a field of view 34’×27’, a unique facility among the the 8-10 m class telescopes, with a resolution of 0.”202 per pixel. ... The wide-field corrector is basically a three-lens Wynne-type, but has a new type of atmospheric dispersion corrector. notes: Explorer conventions used here: F = focal length / pupil diameter of the same configuration (I04 Table 2); plate scale = 206264.8 / f; reflections count mirrors only (correctors and AO optics excluded).

One spider for all foci: the four thick (~0.22-0.24 m) vanes at +/-51.75 deg, offset 0.66 m from the centre, are part of the telescope (top ring + inner ring); the top units (PFU, M2 units) lock into the inner ring (I04). Only the central obscuration changes with the top unit.

The IR secondary (1265 mm) is deliberately undersized: it is the aperture stop at the IR foci (8.08 m Cassegrain, 7.95-7.97 m Nasmyth), keeping warm structure outside the primary out of the IR beam; the published pupil diameters follow from the M2 size and spacing (DERIVED in ir_secondary_stop).

The Nasmyth foci are fed by moving the Opt/Nas or IR M2 along the axis (I04); the paraxial check reproduces every Table 2 focal length and back focus (DERIVED in secondary_mirrors and ir_secondary_nasmyth_use).
